front: Why does atomic radius decrease across a period?
back: Nuclear charge increases while electrons are added to the same shell with similar shielding, so the effective nuclear charge pulls them closer.

front: Why does first IE decrease down a group?
back: The outer electron is in a higher shell, further from the nucleus and more shielded, so less energy is needed to remove it.
Enthalpy change when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of gaseous atoms: X(g) + e⁻ → X⁻(g). Usually exothermic; the second EA is endothermic.
Decreases across a period and increases down a group — follows ease of losing electrons (low IE).

front: Reaction of group 1 metals with water?
back: 2M(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2MOH(aq) + H₂(g); alkaline solution forms. Vigour increases Li < Na < K as IE decreases.
A more reactive halogen oxidises a less reactive halide: Cl₂ + 2KBr → 2KCl + Br₂. Oxidising strength: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.

front: Why does halogen reactivity decrease down group 17?
back: Atoms are larger and outer shell more shielded, so attraction for an incoming electron is weaker.
Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH; MgO + H₂O → Mg(OH)₂ — basic oxides form alkaline solutions.

front: SO₃, P₄O₁₀ and CO₂ with water?
back: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄; P₄O₁₀ + 6H₂O → 4H₃PO₄; CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ — acidic oxides.
Reacts with both acids and bases: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O and Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH + 3H₂O → 2NaAl(OH)₄.

front: Equations forming acid rain from SO₂ and NO₂?
back: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃ (and 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃; SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄). 2NO₂ + H₂O → HNO₂ + HNO₃.
No. It is naturally slightly acidic (pH ≈ 5.6) from dissolved CO₂ forming carbonic acid; acid rain has pH < 5.6.

front: Oxidation states in Cr₂O₇²⁻ and how named?
back: 2x + 7(−2) = −2 → x = +6; dichromate(VI). Roman numerals in names show the oxidation state.

front: Is the oxidation state the same as the ionic charge in covalent species?
back: No. It is a hypothetical charge assuming all bonds are ionic; written sign first (+6), whereas charges are written number first (2+).
An element that has an incomplete d sublevel in the atom or in one or more of its common ions. Zn is not one (Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰).

front: (HL) Why are Sc³⁺ and Zn²⁺ compounds colourless?
back: Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰ and Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰ — no d–d transitions possible.

front: (HL) Why do transition elements show variable oxidation states?
back: 3d and 4s electrons are close in energy, so different numbers can be lost; +2 is common (loss of 4s²).

Ligand: a species with a lone pair that forms a coordination bond to a central metal ion (Lewis base). Coordination number: number of coordination bonds (often 6 → octahedral, 4 → tetrahedral/square planar).

front: (HL) Factors affecting the colour of a complex?
back: Identity of the metal, its oxidation state, the ligand (spectrochemical series) and the geometry — they change the size of the d-orbital splitting ΔE.

front: (HL) Spectrochemical series (data booklet order, weak → strong field)?
back: e.g. I⁻ < Br⁻ < Cl⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < CN⁻ (abridged) — stronger ligands give larger splitting so absorb higher-energy (shorter λ) light.

front: (HL) [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ absorbs orange/red light — what colour is seen?
back: Blue: the complementary colour of the absorbed light (opposite on the colour wheel) is observed.
x + 6(−1) = −3 → x = +3 (CN⁻ ligands each −1). Neutral ligands like H₂O and NH₃ contribute 0.
